result.request_met:
Only one of Lee's four notes is in this review's scope: Step 42. Steps 19-20, 33c and 37 were not assessed here.

Step 42: partly met.

What is better:
- The new view from the front of the case hides most of the buttons' wires behind H4 and behind the board, which is turned away from the camera.
- The USB cable no longer sweeps across the bundles. It touches a wire once, about 1.0 mm at t 0.33, where the first review found 9 contacts.
- The A end's six beats are clean in check_caps.py: no wire or part is entered from t 0.40 to 1.00. It no longer passes through the 4-digit display's wires as it is laid down.
- The lift (beat 1) raises the plug and the Nano Board into no wire.
- Nothing goes under the caption box or off the canvas at any size. Least clearance under the caption box: 8 image px (5 CSS px) at 760 and 16 px (11 CSS px) at 1000, both at t 0.30 and both the dot matrix display's wire arch, not the cable. The cable and A end keep at least 22 px at 760 and 28 px at 1000. At 1920 nothing is within 309 px of the top.

What is not fixed:
- The cable's length still swings like an elastic band, now from 76 to 327 to 117 mm.
- The flat 'paddle' is still there, moved: at the plug at t 0.35, and at the A end at t 0.55-0.65.
- In the module's beats 2-4 (2.4 s), the dot matrix display's wires still visibly pass through the Mini-B plug (up to 4.29 mm), the module (up to 2.99 mm) and the Nano Board, and the bundles cross.
- README states the opposite of the third point.

New confusions from the A end's route:
- It passes behind the top of the module, briefly half-hidden, in its fastest beat.
- It hangs with its tip on the 4-digit display's header, as if plugged into it.
- In the final view it does not read as 'laid on the table'.

So Lee would see fewer cable-through-wire moments than before, but the motion would still look confusing in places.

verdict.reasoning:
The numbers in the finding are right. In steps.json, Step 42 uses usb cable route 118 (75.6 mm). Step 42c then runs through wire_via 230-238 to route 239: 108.5, 156.5, 284.1, 327.2, 225.9, 247.0, 140.5, 117.3, 147.7 and 192.2 mm. Every one of these routes has stretch: true and no tail_from. The player blends stretch routes with sampled(a, n) / sampled(b, n), each bit keeping its share of the length (player.js drawWires, `even`). At each stop the drawn length is the route's own length, so the cable's length really does change on screen.

The first review confirmed this finding. This pass did not address it:
- It fixed the 'paddle' (the LOOP comment in guide.py).
- The tail_from change covers the jumper wires only. usb_held() and turning_layout() still return W.route(..., stretch=True).
- Neither README.txt nor guide.py explains why the length swing was kept.

The finding overstates part of its case:
- **Beats 1-4** (m42_1000_0000 to 0400): the cable's far run goes behind H10 to the A end on the bench. The growth from 75 to 327 mm therefore looks like slack pulled up from behind the case, not like a stretch.
- **Step 43** (192 to 97 mm): this was already the case in round 2 (HEAD steps.json: 167 to 189, the same lengths). The shortened run is again hidden behind the case as the module is lowered.
- **Lee's rulebook** says lead lengths are representative and may change between shapes, stretching evenly (cadasio-patterns.md lines 358 and 388). Changing length is allowed in itself.

The defect that holds up is in the A-end beats, where the whole cable is in view at both ends:
- **Beat 7** (m42_1000_0600 to 0650 to 0700; the same at 760 and 1920, checked in a 0.55-0.75 strip). At 0.6 the cable is a 247 mm sweep over the module's top out to the A end at the upper right. By 0.65 it is a tight hook, the A end hidden behind the plug. At 0.7 it is a 140 mm drop at the left. The cable visibly reels in by about 10 cm in one 0.8 s beat, like a tape measure.
- **Beats 8-10** follow with -23, +30 and +45 mm.

The first-pass frames (verify/motion_Step42c.png, 0.625 to 0.75) show the same pull-in. So it is unresolved, though not worse.

Severity: this is cosmetic. It says nothing wrong about the assembly, and the rulebook tolerates length changes. But it is plainly visible in the step Lee called visually confusing, and it is a confirmed finding left unanswered. So 2.
verdict.fix: Make the change in guide.py USB_A_WAY, and only there. Stops 7-9 are entries [2]-[4] (the A end over the 4-digit display, forward over its pins, lowered). Give them slack by starting their ways with the same LOOP over the module's top that stops 5-6 have (entries [0]-[1]). The near run then stays put and only the far run changes, which adds roughly 50-60 mm to 140/117/148. Also bring stop 6's sweep in (entry [1], its via point [645, 1022, 1356] and the A end at x 680) so it is nearer 200 mm. The aim is stops 5-10 within about 20-25% of each other (about 190-230 mm, ending at the existing 192 mm). Leave beats 1-4 and Step 43 alone: their changing run is hidden behind the case. Then regenerate. Before calling it fixed, re-check Step 42c with check_caps.py (crossings with the display and matrix wires) and the caption box at 760, 1000 and 1920. Alternatively, record in README.txt and rulebook section 13 that Step 42's USB cable keeps the representative-length rule, and say why. Silently leaving it is not enough.

I compared check_caps.py's blending with player.js `skinned()` / `drawWires()`: same ramp, same skinning by end moves, same two-part `tail_from` resample. - `skinned()` moves each point with the module's cap (end b) by `ramp(u)`, which reaches 1 only in the last 10% of the wire. Mid-beat, the run over the plug follows the module only partly.
- The two stage shapes are then blended in a straight line.
